title: SRE Standards: SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity, Incident Reviews, and Runbooks
author: Priya Shah
content:
Overview

This document defines Redwood Inference's SRE standards for Service Level Objectives (SLOs) and error budgets, capacity planning, reliability initiatives, incident review standards, operational tooling, and the canonical SRE runbook format. It is intended for service owners, on-call engineers, product managers, and platform teams responsible for the availability and performance of inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private).

Goals
- Ensure we have clear, measurable SLOs and an operational process for error budget consumption and remediation.
- Provide a repeatable capacity planning and forecasting framework tied to SLOs and customer commitments.
- Standardize incident review procedures to extract actionable reliability improvements.
- Maintain a library of runbooks that are tested, concise, and easily consumable during incidents.
- Standardize operational tooling and metrics used across inference services.

SLO & Error Budget Standards

1) Terminology
- SLI (Service Level Indicator): the measurement used to evaluate a service (e.g., successful request ratio, P95 latency).
- SLO: a commitment expressed as an SLI target over a rolling window (e.g., 99.9% success rate over 30d).
- Error budget: 1 - SLO; the allowable fraction of failures over the SLO window.
- Burn rate: the rate at which the error budget is consumed relative to expectation.

2) SLO definition template (required for every externally facing service)
- Service name: <short service id>
- SLI: <metric name and exact query>
- SLO target: <e.g., 99.95%>
- Window: <e.g., 30d rolling>
- Owner: <team / primary on-call alias>
- Measurement infra: Prometheus metric, retention window, and alerts (see Alerting section)
- Escalation policy: reference to runbook id for threshold breaches

3) Example SLOs (applies to inference endpoints)
Table (rendered as plain text):
| Metric | SLO | Window | Alert threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| API successful request ratio (status in 2xx/5xx/4xx) | 99.90% | 30d rolling | burn-rate > 2 for 6h OR < 99.5% over 1h | inference-api-team |
| P95 server-side latency (in ms) for text-generation | <= 1200ms | 30d rolling | P95 > 1600ms for 10m | runtime-team |
| Embeddings availability (per-region) | 99.95% | 30d rolling | region availability < 99.9% over 1h | dedicated-ops |

4) SLI measurement guidance
- Use explicit, versioned Prometheus queries or event-store counts. Embed the exact query in the SLO document (example below).
- Prefer availability SLIs based on user-visible success (HTTP 200 + non-empty body) rather than infra status.
- Latency SLIs must measure server-side processing time (exclude client or network artifacts when possible).

Example PromQL SLI (availability):
(sum(increase(api_requests_total{job="inference-api",code=~"2.."}[30d])) / sum(increase(api_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[30d]))) * 100

Error budget policy and actions
- Alerting is tiered by burn-rate and remaining budget:
  - Advisory: burn-rate > 1.5 for 3h OR remaining budget < 50% in the window — notify owners, create a ticket (Board: SRE Reliability).
  - Intervention: burn-rate > 2 for 6h OR remaining budget < 25% — require incident review and mitigation plan within 24 hours.
  - Restrictive: burn-rate > 4 OR remaining budget < 10% — freeze non-critical launches, request all-hands from the owning team and platform engineering.
- The owning team must publish a short remediation plan (1–2 paragraphs) within 24 hours for Intervention/Restrictive events.
- If multiple services share a customer-facing SLAs, product and account teams must be notified by the owning SRE.

Capacity Planning and Forecasting

Principles
- Capacity decisions must balance SLO risk, cost, and lead time for procurement or cloud quota increases.
- Forecasts should be driven by usage signals (traffic, concurrency, model sequence length distributions) and product roadmaps.
- Maintain 3 capacity tiers: baseline (steady-state), burst (short-term spikes), and emergency reserve (critical recovery).

Quarterly Capacity Planning Process
1) Inputs (by service owner)
  - Historical traffic (1y preferred, 90d minimum) with percentiles (P50/P90/P99) and sequence length distribution.
  - Upcoming product events, model rollouts, marketing campaigns, and reserved capacity contracts.
  - Recent SLO burn patterns and incidents that affect capacity (e.g., degraded performance).
2) Sizing model (spreadsheet or Terraform variables)
  - Estimate required GPU-hours and memory based on model family, quantization profile, batch sizes, and concurrency targets.
  - Model tail latency impact and set target headroom to meet SLOs (recommended: 20–30% headroom on baseline for critical services).
3) Outputs and approvals
  - Capacity plan (resource increase/decrease, schedule, cost estimate) submitted to Eng Infra and Finance for approval.
  - If additional capacity is needed with >2 week lead time, raise a procurement/quotas request.

Operational tooling for capacity
- Telemetry: Prometheus (metrics), Cortex/Thanos (long-term TS), Grafana dashboards (per-service capacity view).
- Autoscaling and pooling: Kubernetes HPA + custom batch schedulers for GPU pools (see infra runbook).
- Cost tooling: daily cost breakdown by service and model via internal billing pipeline.

Reliability Initiatives and Prioritization

Program cadence
- Each engineering quarter, teams should:
  - Identify top 3 reliability risks (based on SLO burn, incident frequency, and customer impact).
  - Propose one improvement project per quarter (e.g., prefix caching for the top 2 models, KV cache tuning, faster fallback routing).
  - Log projects in the Reliability Initiative board and assign a PM / tech lead.

Initiative criteria (must meet at least one)
- Reduces expected annual outage minutes by > 10% for a high-impact service.
- Reduces token cost variance > 15% for heavy workloads without SLO regression.
- Shortens mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for common failure modes by > 30%.

Incident Review Standards

Scope and timing
- Post-incident reviews (PIRs) are required for any incident that:
  - Exceeded a Severity-2 (S2) threshold or had customer-visible degradation > 30 minutes, OR
  - Consumed > 50% of an error budget in a 24 hour window, OR
  - Caused material revenue impact (billing > $10k deviation)
- PIR must be scheduled within 72 hours and a draft report published within 7 calendar days.

PIR template (minimum sections)
1) Summary — short description, timeline, impact, SLOs affected.
2) Detection and response timeline — what triggered alerts, who responded, and actions taken.
3) Root cause analysis — technical root cause and contributing factors.
4) Corrective actions — immediate fixes and long-term remediation, with owners and ETA.
5) Preventative actions — automation, tests, new metrics, or runbook updates.
6) Follow-up checklist — ensure actions are monitored and closed.

Blameless reviews
- Reviews must be blameless and focus on system/process improvements. Assign one facilitator (not the primary author) and one reviewer from a separate team for cross-checking.

Operational Tooling and Alerts

Canonical metrics (per service)
- availability_ratio (user-visible success)
- request_count_total
- server_processing_time_seconds (histogram)
- kv_cache_hit_ratio
- model_load_time_seconds
- gpu_utilization_percent per pool

Alerting guidelines
- Attach alert runbook links to every alert.
- Use Prometheus alert severity labels: severity=warning, severity=critical.
- Alert thresholds must reference SLO windows and be actionable (i.e., include a clear next step).

Example Prometheus alert:
ALERT SLOErrorBudgetBurnHigh
IF (sum(increase(api_errors_total{job="inference-api"}[1h])) / sum(increase(api_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[1h]))) > 0.005
FOR 30m
LABELS { severity = "warning" }
ANNOTATIONS { summary = "Possible SLO degradation: error rate > 0.5% over 1h", runbook = "confluence/eng-sre/sre-runbooks/inference-api-availability" }

SRE Runbook Standard (canonical structure)
- Runbook ID: <short-id>
- Title: <service + symptom>
- Scope: which endpoints/regions/models are covered
- Preconditions: required permissions, alert IDs, dashboards, and runbook owner
- Immediate checks (first 5 minutes):
  1) Check SLO dashboard and error budget status.
  2) Validate whether the problem is global or region-specific (check region dashboards).
  3) Confirm recent deploys or config changes (CI/CD feed, git commits).
  4) Check infra metrics (GPU pool health, node failures).
  5) If error budget burn is high, run the mitigation sequence.
- Mitigation sequence (example for high error rate):
  1) Apply temporary traffic-split to fallback model variant: `redwood-cli traffic split --from inference-prod --to inference-fallback --percent 20`
  2) Scale up serving pool: `kubectl scale -n inference deployment/runtime --replicas=<n>` (see infra-approved limits).
  3) Clear problematic cache entries: run `redis-cli --eval scripts/clear-prefix.lua <prefix>` (only if safe).
  4) If latency issue, reduce max_sequence_length for requests via the runtime feature flag: `rtctl set param max_seq 1024`
  5) If condition persists after 30 minutes, escalate to paging rotation and platform oncall.
- Post-incident actions: update runbook with anything missing and add unit/regression tests where applicable.

Runbook testing and maintenance
- Every runbook must be reviewed and smoke-tested at least once per quarter by the owning team (game-day exercise).
- Maintain a runbook metadata header: owner, last_tested, test_notes, badge for game-day coverage.

Ownership and governance
- Primary SLO owners are the service product managers and the corresponding SRE on-call alias.
- Eng Infra owns capacity tools and autoscaling infrastructure.
- Reliability Program Manager (RPM) coordinates quarterly reliability initiatives and maintains the Reliability Initiative board.
- SRE Guild reviews and audits SLOs quarterly for drift, tagging potentially stale SLOs for re-evaluation.

Appendices
A) Example SLO declaration (short JSON-style snippet for copy):
Service: inference-api
SLI: availability_ratio (PromQL = `(sum(increase(api_requests_total{job="inference-api",code=~"2.."}[30d])) / sum(increase(api_requests_total{job="inference-api"}[30d]))) * 100`)
SLO: 99.90%
Window: 30d
Owner: inference-api-team@redwood.example.com

B) Quick checklist for on-call escalation
- If alert severity=critical and SLO remaining < 10%: page the owning on-call and platform on-call.
- If a customer SLA is at risk: notify account team, post an incident bridge, and start a PIR timer.

C) Useful links
- SRE runbook index: /confluence/eng-sre/sre-runbooks-index
- Capacity planning spreadsheet template: /confluence/eng-sre/templates/capacity-planning-template
- Reliability Initiative board: /boards/reliability-initiatives

Contact and feedback
- For questions about this standard, contact the SRE Guild (sre-guild@redwood.example.com) or open an issue on the Reliability Initiative board.
